We Work in a Cinema and We Haven't Seen Anything

Three people at the Nurafshon Cinema tell us what they have — and haven't — watched.

ZUHRA, usher. I've worked here for four years. I've seen the first eight minutes of about six hundred films, and the last two minutes of about four hundred, because that's when I go in to open the doors. I've never seen a whole film in this building. My friends think that's very funny. I have been to the cinema across the road twice, though — I bought a ticket like a normal person and I cried at both of them.

KAMOL, projectionist. I've heard every film in here. Heard, not seen. I'm in a small room at the back with a window this big, and after twenty-three years I can tell you which film is playing from the sound alone, in about four seconds. I've forgotten more film music than most people have ever listened to. My daughter has taken me to the cinema exactly once, for my birthday, and I spent the whole evening looking at the ceiling, because that's where the projector is.

MADINA, café. I've read all the reviews, I've written about two hundred of my own online, and I've never paid for a ticket in my life. I watch everything from the doorway, in pieces, while the coffee machine is working. I saw one film in fourteen visits. I still haven't seen the middle of it.

Three people, one building, and between them almost nothing. But ask any of them for a recommendation and you will be there for an hour.

2

Grammar · present perfect

TUSHUNTIRISH — PRESENT PERFECT

Present perfect ni tajriba haqida gapirish uchun ishlatamiz — hayotingizda qachondir boʻlgan, lekin qachon ekanini aytmaydigan narsa.

+ have / has + past participle. They have acted in some very popular films. · Rose has worked for UNICEF. Qisqa shakllar: I've seen it · She's seen it.

− Inkor — not have / has dan KEYIN keladi. I haven't seen the film. · He hasn't read the book.

? Soʻroq — have / has oldin keladi. Have you seen any of her films? · Has he visited Australia? Qisqa javoblar: Yes, I have. / No, I haven't.

ever ever va never past participle dan OLDIN keladi. Have you ever been to a concert? · I've never seen a whole film here.

Qachon ekanini aytmaymiz. ✓ I've seen that film · ✗ I've seen that film last year → I saw that film last year. Vaqtni aytishingiz bilan past simple kerak boʻladi.

Present perfect — tajriba, vaqt aytilmaydi

Past simple — tugagan vaqt

I've seen that film.

I saw it last Friday.

She's worked here for four years.

She started in 2021.

Have you ever been to a concert?

Did you go last summer?

I've never eaten sushi.

I didn't eat anything yesterday.

DIQQAT — KOʻP UCHRAYDIGAN XATOLAR

Besh narsa notoʻgʻri ketadi, oxirgi uchtasi never haqida:

1 Oʻrniga present simple. ✗ I see all of Brad Pitt's films. → ✓ I've seen all of Brad Pitt's films.

2 Notoʻgʻri yordamchi feʼl. ✗ I hasn't been to the USA. → ✓ I haven't been to the USA. I, you, we, they → have. He, she, it → has.

3 ever va never birga. ✗ It's the best film I never ever see. → ✓ It's the best film I have ever seen.

4 never bilan yordamchi feʼlsiz. ✗ I never see a film with Rose Byrne. → ✓ I've never seen a film with Rose Byrne.

5 Ikki inkor. ✗ I never don't see a city like it. → ✓ I've never seen a city like it. never ning oʻzi inkor — unga don't kerak emas.

Vocabulary · irregular past participles

TUSHUNTIRISH — NOTOʻGʻRI FEʼLLAR

Toʻgʻri feʼllarga -ed qoʻshiladi: work → worked → worked. Notoʻgʻri feʼllarga qoʻshilmaydi — ularni yodlash kerak.

Uch shakli bir xil: read → read → read /red/ · had → had · caught → caught · bought → bought · heard → heard

Baʼzilari -en yoki -n bilan tugaydi: break → broke → broken · write → wrote → written · see → saw → seen · eat → ate → eaten · fly → flew → flown · forget → forgot → forgotten · fall → fell → fallen · grow → grew → grown

Va har kuni ishlatadiganingiz: be → was/were → been. I've been to Italy.

read bilan ehtiyot boʻling. U uch marta bir xil yoziladi, lekin oʻtgan shakllari /red/ — rang kabi — aytiladi. I read a lot /riːd/ — har kuni. I've read it /red/ — qachondir.

FIKR SOʻRASH VA BILDIRISH

Soʻrash: So, what did you think of it? · Did you enjoy it? · How about you?

Javob berish: Yeah, it was a good concert. · I really liked it.

Eng yaxshidan eng yomongacha uch daraja:

I really liked the first band. → I didn't like the first band very much. → I didn't like the first band at all.

Keyin sabab ayting. Yolgʻiz fikr suhbatni toʻxtatadi; I thought… bilan aytilgan fikr esa uni davom ettiradi. I really liked them — I thought the singer was great.

FIKRGA JAVOB BERISH

Kimdir fikr bildiradi. Munosabat bildirishga taxminan bir soniyangiz bor, shuning uchun ingliz tilida ikki soʻzli javoblar ishlatiladi:

Rozi boʻlsangiz — I liked it. → Me too. · I didn't like it. → Me neither.

Hayron boʻlsangiz va unchalik rozi boʻlmasangiz — I liked it. → Did you? · I think they're great. → Do you?

have emas, do yoki did ishlating. Va javob berayotgan gapingizdagi zamonni ishlating: I liked it. → Did you? · I like them. → Do you?

Ehtiyot boʻling: Me neither inkorga javob beradi. Kimdir I didn't like it desa va siz Me too desangiz, uning aytganining teskarisiga rozi boʻlgan boʻlasiz.

TALAFFUZ — ASOSIY URGʻU VA OHANG

Bu javoblarda ikkala soʻz ham urgʻuli — DO YOU? · DID YOU? · ME TOO. · ME NEITHER.

Yoʻnalish — maʼno. Do you? ↗ va Did you? ↗ koʻtariladi — siz hayronsiz. Me too. ↘ va Me neither. ↘ pasayadi — siz rozisiz.

Did you? ni pasayuvchi ovoz bilan aytsangiz, zerikkan yoki jahli chiqqandek eshitilasiz — siz buni nazarda tutmagansiz. Barcha xushmuomalalikni koʻtarilish bajaradi.

5.5 Up (↗) or down (↘)? Then say each one.

Koʻtariladimi (↗) yoki pasayadimi (↘)? Keyin har birini ayting.

1 Do you?

3 Me too.

2 Did you?

4 Me neither.

5.6 Read the model, then answer.

Namunani oʻqing, keyin javob bering.

MODEL

AZIZA So, what did you think of it?

TIMUR Yeah, it was a good concert. I really liked it. How about you?

AZIZA I liked it, but I didn't like all the bands. I didn't like the first one very much — I thought the songs were all the same.

TIMUR Did you? I thought they were quite good. The singer was excellent.

AZIZA She was, yes. But the last band were too loud for me.

TIMUR Me too, actually. My ears are still ringing. … Have you heard their album?

AZIZA No, I haven't. And after tonight, I'm not going to.
